profile.what: Citigroup is the most global US bank, serving multinational companies in about 90 countries through treasury, trade and securities services, plus US credit cards and wealth management. It is in a multi-year restructuring and is exiting most consumer banking outside the US.
profile.money: Net interest income and fees from moving money for multinationals (its treasury and trade business), plus card interest, investment banking and trading. Restructuring costs and regulatory penalties have kept returns below its peers'.
profile.valued: Citi trades at a discount to tangible book value because its returns have been below its cost of capital. The stock rises with progress toward its return target, which would close that discount.
profile.peer_group: Financials · bank, insurer or asset manager

summary.sentence: A global bank partway through a long restructuring, priced below its book value.
risks: Return on equity is only about 8%.

meaning.what_it_does: A global bank serving multinationals, with US cards and wealth management.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: Fees for moving money for corporations, trading, and interest on loans and cards.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: Its global payments network for multinationals is unique.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: The long-running restructuring fails to lift returns.

moat.summary: A valuable global network inside a bank that has under-earned for fifteen years.

valuation.method: Banks are valued on book value, not free cash flow. Justified price-to-book = (ROE − 3% growth) ÷ (required return − 3%), using a normalised ROE of 5.8% (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM, capped at 25%) and a required return of 11% (low) to 9% (high): 0.35–0.46 × book value per share of $127.58.

methods.name: Excess-return model on book value
methods.basis: Book value per share $127.58 × 0.35–0.46. This is how Damodaran values banks and insurers: equity is worth book value plus the returns earned above the cost of equity.
